title: Four Thousand Miles across Siberia
subtitle: On the Great Post-Road
edition_statement: Every Age Library edition, with a new preface (London, 1909; the title page is undated, the preface is dated 1909); first published in 1896 as Across Siberia on the Great Post-Road

divisions.title: The book’s title above Chapter I

summary: Charles Wenyon, a medical missionary in China, went home to England across Siberia in the spring and summer of 1893 (his preface of 1909 dates the journey sixteen years back). He landed at Vladivostock and went by tarantass to Lake Khanka, where he waited in a village for the ice to break; by steamer down the Usuri and up the Amoor and the Shilka; on the great post-road over the plateau and Lake Baikal, through Irkutsk to Tomsk; by river to Tiumen; and by railway over the Urals to the German frontier, where he was detained on suspicion.

He describes post-stations, drivers, and roads, Siberian villages, a church service and a wedding, Cossacks, Buriats, Tungus, and Ostiaks, and exiles and convicts on the road. This is the reissue of 1909, with a new preface written after the railway had replaced the road.
